newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon attends security aviation conference.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon attends security aviation conference.

text.p: Lebanon will participate in a U.S.-sponsored conference on civil aviation security and safety in the hope this can help ease or lift a 10-year-old U.S. travel ban on the country.
Beirut airport sources said Lebanese Director General for Civil Aviation Riad Abdallah left for Washington on Saturday to attend the annual international conference on aviation safety and security.
Through its Beirut embassy, the United States had urged Lebanon to attend next week's conference, which will provide a chance to reevaluate the state of security at Beirut airport.

After the conference, the White House Commission for Safety and Security Aviation, headed by U.S. Vice President Al Gore, will report to the U.S. president on the state of aviation security in each of the participating countries.

Sources in the ministry of transportation believe this might help ease or lift a 10-year-old travel ban on Lebanon imposed by the Washington after a series of hijacks and kidnappings of Westerners by militia groups at the height of the civil war.
The ban, which comes up for review every six month, is next scheduled for scrutiny in February.
